issues.display_title: Issue #108: Directory: type a city to search, auto-fill continent/country, and invite to join when a place has no photographers
issues.main_description_html:
Demo by Developer

video-108-directory-city-search.mp4

Problem

Client feedback on the directory's "Search the directory" card:

This filter is way to hard to use and it looks like it does not work. I should be able to just type New Orleans and reach that place. Why I need to select North America > United States > New Orleans? and I don't get anything. If there are no photographers, we should display a page maybe no photographer and invite to join the list.

I should be able to just type the city and the country, continent auto fill based on the city.

What happens today (src/components/directory-page.tsx):

  • The filter is a strict cascade. Continent → Country → City, and City stays disabled until a country is picked.
  • The City list only has cities with at least one published 360 photographer. This comes from the backend ActiveCities scope behind v1/geodata/cities. On dev, United States has 36. New Orleans has no photographer, so typing it shows "No results" with no reason given. It looks broken, but it is working as built.
  • An empty list says "No matches / Try widening the filters or clearing your search." (directory-page.tsx:544-548). There's no hint that the place just has no photographers yet, and no way to join.

The backend already returns everything needed for a type-a-city search. GET v1/photographers/search/location?q= (searchLocation() in src/data/layer/photographers.ts) returns { city, country, continent } with ids and counts for each match. The map page uses it with a 300 ms debounce and fills the whole location from the picked result (src/components/map-page.tsx:345-366). The directory page doesn't use it. No backend change is needed.

Scope

  1. City search on the directory card. Add a type-ahead input ("Search a city…") above the cascade. Reuse the map page's searchLocation pattern: 300 ms debounce, at least 3 characters.
    • Picking a result sets continentName/continentId, countryId and cityId. It also loads the countries and cities lists, so the three selects show the picked place and can still be changed by hand.
    • Then run the same search as the Search button: list, total, URL via pushCountryUrl, and the map MAP_RECV_LOCATION / MAP_LOAD_LOCATION_MARKER.
    • Keep the cascade as it is, for browsing.
  2. No match for a typed city. search/location returns 404 "No locations found". The dropdown should say No photographers in "" yet, with a join link instead of a bare "No results". The endpoint only matches cities that have photographers, so a typo and an unserved city look the same. The message has to cover both.
  3. Empty list state. When a location filter is applied and the list is empty, replace "Try widening the filters…" with "No photographers in <city/country> yet". Add an invite to join, using the same target as the header's "Join Now" (https://gothru.co), plus a Reset filters button. With no filter, keep the current copy.
  4. Optional: the City select's own "No results" (GeoSelect, directory-page.tsx:707-711) could say "No photographers in this city yet" for the City field.

Verify

  • Type new y → "New York City, United States". Pick it → Continent = North America, Country = United States, City = New York City, and the list and map show its photographers.
  • Type new orleans → "No photographers in "new orleans" yet" with a join link. No crash and no stuck spinner.
  • Pick a city, then change the Country select by hand → the City resets like today.
  • Reset clears the city search input too.
  • Filter to a place with no photographers → the empty state shows the place name and the join CTA. With no filter, the empty state is unchanged.
  • /virtual-tour-services-<country> landing pages still seed the Country select and its cities like today.

issues.display_title: Issue #103: LinkedIn review: slug-based form on /photographer/[slug]/review using /review/submit
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

Backend gothru-maps-backend-go#122 (issue #27) adds a stable, slug-based way to review a photographer. As of c766672 the change is additive:

  • New: POST /v1/photographers/review/submit takes { slug, rating, comment } plus the linkedin_auth cookie. The reviewer's name and email come from the LinkedIn profile. If this LinkedIn account already reviewed the photographer, it returns 409 and does not overwrite the review.
  • New: GET /v1/photographers/:identifier/review/link returns the stable /photographer/<slug>/review URL. No login is needed.
  • Unchanged: POST /review/linkedin/link still returns /review/<code> (with the 24h rule and 409), and POST /review/linkedin/:code still submits or updates through the code form.

Today the frontend only uses the code flow. /photographer/[slug]/review (PhotographerReviewEntry) shows only the LinkedIn button and the email option, with no form and no detection of a signed-in user.

Scope

  1. /photographer/[slug]/review: call getLinkedInProfile() server-side.
    • Valid session: render the review form (rating + comment). Reuse photographerReview.tsx and ReviewIdentityHeader where they fit.
    • No session: keep today's entry page.
  2. Add a data-layer call for internal:post:v1/photographers/review/submit (src/data/apiRoutes.ts + photographers.linkedin.ts).
    • Forward only linkedin_auth, the way submitLinkedInReview does.
    • Send slug in the body. The BE's linkedin_oauth_slug cookie fallback is never set through the FE proxy.
  3. Handle the responses:
    • 200 → /photographer/[slug]/review/complete
    • 401 → login prompt (review/error?reason=session_expired)
    • 409 → "you already reviewed this photographer" message. Updating still goes through the code flow, so link to it or to the profile.
    • 400/404 → existing error page
  4. Decide whether auth/linkedin/complete/route.ts keeps redirecting to /review/<code> or switches to the slug page. Either works now. Switch only once this form ships.

Dependencies / order

  • Blocked on backend #122 merging into development (approved 2026-10-07). Then test the local FE against a BE that has /review/submit.
  • Old /review/<code> links that were already sent must keep working. Don't touch the code flow here.

Verify

  • Not signed in: /photographer/<slug>/review shows the LinkedIn button, same as today.
  • Signed in (LinkedIn login → callback → complete): the slug page shows the form, with no loop.
  • Submit → complete page, and the review appears on the profile.
  • A second submit from the same LinkedIn account gets a 409 message, not a crash, and no duplicate review.
  • An expired or missing linkedin_auth on submit gets a 401 and a login prompt.
  • The existing /review/<code> flow still works.

Related: #98, #100 (LinkedIn cookie relay).

issues.display_title: Issue #100: LinkedIn: forwarded Cookie header can be split by ';' in decoded cookie values
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

getForwardCookieHeader (src/data/helpers.ts:81-87) builds the Cookie header that is sent to the backend from cookies().getAll(), and joins each entry as ${name}=${value}. Next decodes cookie values when it reads them (decodeURIComponent) and only encodes them on set. So a decoded value that contains ; splits into extra cookies in the forwarded header.

oauth_return holds window.location.href (saveOAuthReturnUrl). A ; in the page URL, e.g. ?x=;linkedin_oauth_state=<value>, is stored as %3B, decoded back to ; on read, and forwarded as a separate linkedin_oauth_state=<value> cookie.

Once backend gothru-maps-backend-go#120 enforces state == linkedin_oauth_state, an injected value can satisfy that check. That makes a login CSRF possible: the victim ends up signed in with the attacker's LinkedIn account. The same split can also inject any other cookie name the backend reads.

Callers: completeLinkedInCallback and getLinkedInProfile (src/data/layer/photographers.linkedin.ts, forwardRequestCookies: true).

Fix

Forward the browser's raw cookie request header ((await headers()).get('cookie')) instead of re-serializing decoded values. This is what the old src/data/linkedin-callback-server.ts did before be6dcd2. Encoding each value with encodeURIComponent would also work.

Check: no caller depends on a cookie that cookies().set() wrote earlier in the same request, because the raw header won't contain it.

Verify

  • Seed oauth_return with a URL that contains ;linkedin_oauth_state=evil. Confirm the header sent to the backend carries a single linkedin_oauth_state (the real one) or none.
  • LinkedIn login → callback → /auth/linkedin/complete still works end to end.

Related: #98 / #99.

Implemented Security Fix getForwardCookieHeader() reads incoming raw (await nextHeaders()).get('cookie') ?? '' without re-encoding mutations

Responsiveness Verified review landing page at 375px mobile viewport

1. Technical Evaluation & Verification

  • Raw Cookie Header Forwarding: In src/data/helpers.ts, getForwardCookieHeader was refactored: 
    // Fixed in helpers.ts:
async function getForwardCookieHeader(): Promise<string> {
  return (await nextHeaders()).get('cookie') ?? '';
}
    This eliminates the risk where cookies().getAll() returned auto-decoded cookies (decodeURIComponent) where characters like %3B became raw ;, splitting single cookies into multiple fake headers on join('; ').
  • Mitigation of State Forgery & Login CSRF: Injected values in oauth_return (which stores the target return URL) can no longer inject or override linkedin_oauth_state. The raw cookie string preserves percent-encoded delimiters as passed from the browser.
  • Header State Isolation: Confirmed that initiating OAuth via /api/auth/linkedin generates an isolated, valid UUID for linkedin_oauth_state marked HttpOnly and SameSite=Lax.

issues.display_title: Issue #98: LinkedIn login: pass linkedin_oauth_state cookie through /api/auth/linkedin
issues.main_description_html:
Problem

GET /api/auth/linkedin (src/app/api/auth/linkedin/route.ts) fetches the backend's /v1/auth/linkedin server-side with redirect: 'manual', then returns NextResponse.redirect(location). That is a fresh response, so the backend's Set-Cookie: linkedin_oauth_state=<uuid> never reaches the browser.

Backend PR gothru-maps-backend-go#120 (issue #30) restores the OAuth CSRF check, which requires the state query param to equal the linkedin_oauth_state cookie on /v1/auth/linkedin/callback. Without this fix, every LinkedIn login on prod would return 400 "Invalid state parameter. Possible CSRF attack." and land on the linkedin_error page.

Evidence (2026-10-07):

  • curl -I https://360photographers.org/api/auth/linkedin → 307 to LinkedIn, no set-cookie
  • curl -I http://192.168.1.194:3008/v1/auth/linkedin → 302 with Set-Cookie: linkedin_oauth_state=…

Fix

Copy the backend's Set-Cookie headers onto the redirect response in route.ts. The callback leg already forwards the browser's cookies (completeLinkedInCallback → forwardRequestCookies: true), so it needs no change.

Release order

  1. This FE fix is merged and deployed to prod (manual).
  2. Only then promote backend #120 from development to main, which auto-deploys to prod.

Out of scope (follow-up)

getForwardCookieHeader (src/data/helpers.ts) re-joins Next-decoded cookie values without re-encoding them, so a ; inside oauth_return can inject extra cookies into the header sent to the backend. This one needs its own fix.

issues.display_title: Issue #119: Directory: Algeria search returns 0 results but map displays active pin
issues.main_description_html:
Problem & Description

When searching the directory for photographers in Africa > Algeria, the directory card and listing report 0 photographers and render the empty state:

No photographers yet
No photographers in Algeria yet.
Know the area? Join the directory and be the first one listed here.
[Join the directory] [Reset filters]

However, on the embedded interactive map right above the list, an active photographer marker is visible in Algeria. Clicking the marker opens a valid photographer popup:

  • Photographer: Youcef Pnl
  • Location: Oran, Algeria (Main location)
  • Profile: Verified Google Street View Trusted Photographer in Oran, Algeria

This creates an inconsistency where the map displays an active photographer pin, but the directory index counter and photographer list report 0 results and claim nobody is listed in Algeria yet.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Navigate to the Directory homepage (https://360photographers.org/ or http://localhost:3000/).
  2. In the "Search the directory" card:
    • Select Continent: Africa
    • Select Country: Algeria
  3. Click the Search button.
  4. Observe the directory counter and the cards list below the map:
    • Counter shows 0 results / 0 Photographers.
    • Empty state renders: "No photographers in Algeria yet".
  5. Observe the map embed positioned directly above the list:
    • There is an active marker pinned in Algeria.
    • Clicking the marker displays photographer "Youcef Pnl" (Oran, Algeria).

Expected Behavior

  • If a photographer (e.g., Youcef Pnl) is registered and plotted in Algeria on the map, the directory search for Algeria should display 1 results and list their photographer card.
  • If the photographer is not published or unlisted, their pin should not be visible on the public map.
  • The directory index count and the map markers must strictly agree.

Actual Behavior

  • Directory list displays 0 results with the empty state inviting users to join.
  • Map displays 1 active pin in Oran, Algeria pointing to a verified photographer.

Technical Investigation & Suspected Root Cause

  1. Role / Status Filtering Mismatch in Backend:
    • The directory list queries GET /v2/photographers/users?continentId=1&countryId=4 (filtering by role=photographer_360), whereas the map embed loads markers from the map socket/service cache (MAP_PHOTOGRAPHERS_MARKERS_VISIBLE / MAP_LOAD_LOCATION_MARKER).
    • If a photographer has a profile record or sublocation associated with country ID 4 (Algeria) but does not have the active flags required by /v2/photographers/users or is classified under a different country ID in one table, the map markers query (/v1/photographers/count or map database) includes them while /v2/photographers/users filters them out.
  2. Geodata Country ID Linkage:
    • Need to verify if Youcef Pnl's country_id in database matches the dropdown ID for Algeria (id: 4) or if there is a discrepancy in how agency sublocations/cities are assigned.

issues.display_title: Issue #120: Find Photographers: 'Featured photographer' badge text is dark and unreadable in dark mode
issues.main_description_html:
Problem & Description

On the Find Photographers page (/find-google-trusted-photographers), when dark mode is enabled, the "Featured photographer" badge label and star icon on cards in the side list appear as near-black text on a dark card background (bg-card).

This creates a serious contrast failure (near-zero contrast ratio), rendering the "Featured photographer" text unreadable in dark mode.

Steps to Reproduce

  1. Open the Find Photographers page (https://360photographers.org/find-google-trusted-photographers or http://localhost:3000/find-google-trusted-photographers).
  2. Toggle the theme to Dark Mode via the theme toggle button in the header.
  3. Observe the side list of photographers under "Nearby photographers" (or check the "Featured only" toggle to isolate featured cards).
  4. Inspect the "Featured photographer" text under cards such as Christopher Riddell or IL Ian Lewis.

Expected Behavior

  • In dark mode, badge labels and highlights should maintain sufficient contrast against dark card backgrounds (e.g. using light accent text like text-primary, text-accent, or gold/amber #f59e0b / text-yellow-400).

Actual Behavior

  • The text and star icon are rendered in a dark tone (oklch(0.147 0.004 49.25)), making it invisible/unreadable against the dark theme background.

Technical Details & Root Cause

In src/components/map-page.tsx:683:

{p.featured && (
  <div className="mt-1.5 flex items-center gap-1 font-mono text-[10px] uppercase tracking-wider text-accent-foreground">
    <Star className="size-2.5 fill-current" /> Featured photographer
  </div>
)}

The element applies text-accent-foreground. In src/app/globals.css, dark mode defines:

.dark {
  --accent:              oklch(0.72 0.120 196);
  --accent-foreground:   oklch(0.147 0.004 49.25); /* <-- near black! */
}

Because --accent-foreground is intended for text placed on top of --accent background, using it directly on bg-card in dark mode renders almost pitch black.

Recommended Fix:

Change text-accent-foreground in map-page.tsx:683 to a theme-aware contrast color such as text-accent, text-primary, or text-amber-500 dark:text-amber-400.
